title.analysis: Authentic title "Why Your First Million Feels Impossible (And The Next Comes Fast)" pairs a pain point with a reassuring compounding payoff. The script delivers the compounding-milestone math (9/6/4/3 years) plus psychology, debt and systems. The title's "next comes fast" is supported only with no withdrawals and steady 8% returns, and the opening "about three years" contradicts the video's own 9-year figure. STRONG against the cohort (borderline, about 2.08x). Association only.

script.opening_words: Picture this scenario. You're scrolling through social media, watching people your age buying luxury cars, taking expensive vacations, and seemingly living their best financial lives. Meanwhile, you're calculating whether you can afford both groceries and gas this week. The gap between where you are and that magical 7 figure milestone feels wider than the Grand Canyon. But here's something that might surprise you about millionaires that nobody talks about. Most of them didn't earn their second million by grinding for
script.ending_words: it. The first million is brutal because you're essentially paying tuition to learn how money actually works while fighting against your own psychology and limited resources. But once you've earned that financial PhD and compound interest starts doing the heavy lifting, subsequent millions practically fall into your lap. Now stop scrolling through social media comparing yourself to others and start building systems that will make your future self disgustingly wealthy.
script.analysis: Full 20143 canonical characters read. A single-narrator motivational explainer: social-media comparison hook; claim that later millions come in ~3 years; channel pitch; why the first million is hard (learning, mistakes, fear, low risk tolerance); millionaires' risk cushion; good vs bad debt; access to capital and opportunities; contributions vs compounding ($5,000 saved vs $80,000 growth); milestone timing (9/6/4/3 years); mindset shift; assets vs liabilities; tax incentives; systems over goals; emotions; 8% vs 10% returns; time as ally; pattern recognition; exclusive investments; start early ($300 at 25 vs $1,000 at 45); growth at $2-4M; financial vertigo; close. Most arithmetic reproduces. Errors: the opening "second million in about three years" contradicts the 9-year math; 2->3M takes 5.3 years, not 6; "lower fees" for hedge funds/PE is wrong; "inflation becomes less relevant" is misleading. The stored ending is complete.
